title: Persistent tenant usage bleed after service-mesh token swap
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers reported consumption spikes and quota overruns after an automated token swap flow ran during a service-mesh rollout. Investigation shows a class of requests issued with rotated tokens were attributed to parent org IDs instead of the originating subaccount/project for a multi-hour window. This ticket captures the investigation, reproduction steps, temporary mitigations, and proposed long-term fix to prevent cross-tenant attribution drift during token/key rotations and service-mesh proxy swaps.

Observed behavior: When token exchange (rotation) occurred mid-flight while the new mesh sidecar started routing, the attribution layer sometimes resolved the request principal to the legacy owner context. Result: tenant A usage billed to tenant B (parent org), token-level quotas enforced against wrong workspace, rate-limiter counters incremented in the incorrect tenant bucket.

Scope: Impacted 6 customers (2 enterprise, 4 mid-market) with dedicated subaccounts between 2026-03-11 22:14 UTC and 2026-03-12 02:40 UTC. Rough estimate of misattributed tokens: ~3.2M tokens total; financial exposure under investigation in Finance.

Why this ticket: root-cause hypothesis points to a race between the token-rotation response path and the service-mesh sidecar's identity cache invalidation. We need a reproducible test, a short-term mitigation to stop further drift, and a safe rollout plan for the attribution fix with traceable fallbacks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a multi-tenant stack with parent org, child workspace, and an integration token that will be rotated via the automated rotation service.
2) Configure service-mesh sidecar that performs per-request principal lookups and caches owner mapping for 10s.
3) Start a burst of requests (~500 RPS) from the client using the pre-rotation token.
4) Trigger token rotation (simulate rotation API call) mid-burst so some requests complete while token swap is in-flight.

5) Observe attribution logs in /var/log/redwood/attribution.log and meter inserts to billing-db.transactions. Look for mismatches where request_id maps to original token but billing tenant_id is parent org id.
6) Example log snippet to search for: 'request_id=... principal=token_abc owner_id=org:parent::123 resolved_owner=org:parent::123 (expected workspace: ws:child::456)'.
impact_summary: High customer impact: quota/enforcement violations and incorrect billing records. Some customers hit hard quota limits and experienced request throttles that should have applied to a child workspace, causing degraded service. Finance flagged potential overbilling; customer success notified affected accounts.
root_cause: Preliminary analysis: race condition between token-rotation endpoint and service-mesh identity cache invalidation. The attribution pipeline resolves owner metadata in two stages: (A) token principal lookup (auth service) and (B) owner enrichment in the mesh proxy using cached mappings. When rotation occurs, the auth service issued a short-lived transitional principal that the attribution join logic used, but the mesh proxy returned stale owner metadata (parent org) for a subset of requests. There is no final canonical reconciliation step before writing meter entries. Contributing factors: cache TTL too long (10s), attribution write path trusts immediate join of auth+mesh without cross-check, and lack of idempotent attribution markers in the metering API.
mitigation:
Immediate actions taken: 1) Rolled back mesh sidecar config to use strict owner validation mode (disables cached owner read) for affected clusters — completed 2026-03-12 08:03 UTC. 2) Disabled automatic token rotation for high-risk tenants until patch — completed 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC. 3) Ran a reconciliation job to identify likely misattributed transactions and flagged them with 'pending_reconciliation' tag in billing-db (work in progress).

Operational guardrails to implement ASAP: - Add server-side attribution double-check: before persisting meter records, validate owner_id against token principal via authoritative lookup with short timeout (200ms) and fail closed (reject write) if mismatch detected. - Reduce attribution cache TTL to 500ms by default for rotated tokens. - Emit structured tracing fields for token rotation events to make post-hoc reconciliation possible.
proposed_fix:
Long-term fix plan: 1) Add atomic attribution resolution service (single RPC) that returns canonical owner_id for a given request_id/token; ensure this service reads authoritative token registry and workspace graph with linearizable read. 2) Make metering writes require the attribution service token (attribution_id) as proof of owner resolution. 3) Update service-mesh sidecars to consult new attribution service rather than local cache for requests during known rotation windows. 4) Add migration job that reprocesses transactions with 'pending_reconciliation' using audit logs and traces to correct billing records. 5) Include e2e test coverage in CI simulating simultaneous token rotations and high QPS.

Rollout plan: canary to non-production, then 10% production traffic, then 100% after 48h monitoring. Include automatic fallback to previous attribution path on elevated reconciliation failures.
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative attribution RPC implemented and documented
Metering write path validates owner via attribution RPC within 200ms and rejects ambiguous attributions
Reconciliation job can locate and correct >=95% of flagged transactions in a test dataset
E2E stress tests for rotation+routing pass in CI with no misattributions in 100k-request test
Operational runbook updated and Customer Success notified with remediation templates
